items.title: EoP Flaws Again Lead Microsoft Patch Day
items.description: Nearly half the CVEs Microsoft disclosed in its September security update, including one publicly known bug, enable escalation of privileges.

items.title: U.S. sanctions cyber scammers who stole billions from Americans
items.description: The U.S. Department of the Treasury has sanctioned several large networks of cyber scam operations in Southeast Asia, which stole over $10 billion from Americans last year. [...]

items.title: Is the Browser Becoming the New Endpoint?
items.description: While the jury is still out on whether the browser is the new endpoint, it's clear that use has skyrocketed and security needs to align.

items.title: Qantas Reduces Executive Pay Following Cyberattack
items.description: The data breach, which occurred earlier this year, saw threat actors compromise a third-party platform to obtain Qantas customers' personal information.

items.title: Hackers hide behind Tor in exposed Docker API breaches
items.description: A threat actor targeting exposed Docker APIs has updated its malicious tooling with more dangerous functionality that could lay the foundation for a complex botnet. [...]

items.title: Microsoft Patches 86 Vulnerabilities
items.description: Microsoft has released patches for dozens of flaws in Windows and other products, including ones with ‘exploitation more likely’ rating. The post Microsoft Patches 86 Vulnerabilities appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Huge NPM Supply-Chain Attack Goes Out With Whimper
items.description: Threat actors phished Qix's NPM account, then used their access to publish poisoned versions of 18 popular open-source packages accounting for more than 2 billion weekly downloads.

items.title: Adobe Patches Critical ColdFusion and Commerce Vulnerabilities
items.description: Adobe has patched nearly two dozen vulnerabilities across nine of its products with its September 2025 Patch Tuesday updates. The post Adobe Patches Critical ColdFusion and Commerce Vulnerabilities appeared first on SecurityWeek.
